children: The following diagrams outline of how replenishment can be used in your warehouse:
Replenishment to Satisfy Item/Location Demand Resulting From RF Outbound Short Picks

This process diagram illustrates how the system creates replenishment 
 requests for pool or wave needs. Each step in the process diagram is further 
 explained in the descriptions below. To access a specific description, 
 click on either the number or the step in the diagram. The system will 
 navigate to the description. To review all of the descriptions, use the 
 toolbar to scroll through them.

Step 1: Replenishment is initiated from either the wave cycle or the 
Inventory Insight.

If the replenishment is initiated 
 from a wave, the system retrieves all of the replenishment master 
 records with the 'wave' replenishment mode. It sorts the records in priority 
 order. Later, these records are processed in priority order: the lower 
 the priority number, the sooner it is run.

If the replenishment 
 is initiated from the Inventory Insight, the system will display 
 the Manual Replenishment screen. The user will select the replenishment 
 master records that he/she wants to run.
Step 2: The system determines what items are eligible for replenishment.

The system obtains the first replenishment master, based on priority, 
 and references its replenishment type. The type defined here determines 
 where the system will check for possible replenishment.

If the Use Demand from Pool 
 type is selected, the system will check for replenishment opportunities 
 in the order pool.

If the Use 
 Demand from Wave type is selected, the system will check for replenishment 
 opportunities in a wave being run. In this case, replenishment opportunities 
 are only retrieved for this one wave.

The system identifies which items to consider for replenishment 
 based on the values defined on the Filter By Tab on the Replenishment 
 Item Criteria Window. If an item in the pool/wave meets the criteria defined 
 on the replenishment item criteria record, it is considered eligible for 
 replenishment.

The system organizes all items that it retrieves based on the values 
 defined on the Order By Tab on the replenishment item criteria record.
Step 3: The system determines if replenishment is required.

The system retrieves the demand UM values and the replenishment 
 increment value from the replenishment master record.

It uses the demand UMs to 
 determine what unit of measures need to be replenished. For example, if 
 the demand UM is each, the system will only attempt to replenish requests 
 for eaches. Requests for the same item in different units of measure are 
 ignored.

If there are multiple demands using different unit of measures, the system converts the request to the lowest unit of measure on the demands and adds them together. It then performs one replenishment for the total demand amount and converts it back to the different UMs.

It uses the 
 replenishment increment to determine what unit of measure to replenish 
 the requests in. This can be a different UM than the Demand UM. For example, 
 you may want to satisfy each demand only (demand UM), but need to move 
 cases forward (replenishment increment).

The system determines what units of measure and quantities were 
 requested for the items eligible for replenishment.

If necessary, the system performs UM conversions upwards within 
 a detail. For example, if a detail requests 30 eaches and there are 20 
 eaches in a case, the system would convert this request to 1 case 10 eaches. 
 The system never performs UM conversions outside of a detail as the quantities 
 might be destined for different customers.

All quantities in the same unit of measure as 
 the Demand UM (Step A) are eligible for replenishment. In Step B above, 
 if the Demand UM is Each, the 10 eaches would be eligible for replenishment. 
 The 1 case is not eligible for replenishment since the Demand UM does 
 not include cases. The system converts this quantity based on the replenishment 
 increment (Step A). In Step B, if the replenishment increment is Case, 
 the system would attempt to replenish 1 case (10 eaches in a case).

Step 4: The system determines if the quantity needed is available in 
 the 'replenishment locations'.

The system identifies which locations it should attempt to replenish 
 product to. The system reviews the locations defined on the Replenishment 
 Location Criteria Window. Do any of these locations currently contain 
 this product?

If yes, the system will 
 begin replenishment at these locations.

If no, 
 the system will reference the replenishment empty location criteria record 
 associated with this replenishment master. This record identifies where 
 the system should locate replenished product if the replenishment locations 
 are either filled or don't contain the product.

After the system identifies the replenishment locations, 
 it determines how many On Hand units of the requested product they contain.

The system compares the locations' total On Hand quantity with the 
 requested quantity.

If the locations' quantity 
 is greater than the request's quantity, replenishment is not required 
 for this item request. If more items were requested in this pool/wave, 
 the system will attempt to replenish them. Return to Step 2B.

If the location's 
 quantity is less than the request's quantity, the system will check 
 the quantity available in a replenishment is triggered. Continue to Step 
 5.

Step 5: The system finds a location that can support the requested 
 quantity.

For the first location available, the system determines how many 
 units it can hold. The system accesses the Item Location Capacity record 
 to determine how many units the first location can hold. It will reference 
 the Maximum Quantity Field on this window.

If the Maximum Quantity is 
 defined, the system uses it (and the UM Field) to determine how 
 many units this location can hold.

If the Maximum Quantity is 
 not defined, the system calculates how many units the location 
 can hold. It performs this calculation by completing the following:

It compares the location's dimensions to the item's dimensions. 
 The location dimensions are stored on the location type record. The item 
 dimensions are stored for either the item or its item class on the item 
 unit of measure record.

Maximum Quantity = (Location Length / 
 Item Length) x (Location Width / Item Width) x (Location Height / Item 
 Height) or (Location Length / Item Width) x (Location Width / Item Length) 
 x (Location Height / Item Height), whichever is greater.

children: How the System Calculates Maximum Quantity based on Dimensions:

The example below describes how the system will calculate maximum 
 quantity based on item and location dimensions. For this example, suppose 
 the location's dimensions are 40 x 20 x 10. The item's dimensions are 
 7 x 4 x 8.

The system will calculate how many units can be stored in this location 
 by comparing the item's dimensions to the location's dimensions.

This will tell the system how many units can fit across the location 
 per dimension. The system will always round down and arrive at a whole 
 number for each calculation.

Second, 
 the system calculates how many units can fit if the item is placed in 
 sideways.

The system compares these two calculations and accepts the largest 
 one, 25. It will consider 25 the maximum number of units for this item/location.

After the system identifies how much product this location can hold, 
 it determines if it can be replenished by completing the following:

The system determines the location's percentage of fullness, 
 by dividing the On Hand and In Transit Quantities (Step 3) by the Maximum 
 Quantity (Step 4).

It compares this percentage to the value defined in the Minimum 
 Replenishment Threshold Field on the Item Location Capacity record.

If this amount is equal to or less than value 
 defined in the Minimum Replenishment Threshold Field, the system will 
 trigger a replenishment for this location.

Step 6: The system uses the strategies to determine how much to replenish 
 the location.

If a replenishment is required, the system uses the strategies defined 
 on the replenishment master record. Currently, the system supports three 
 strategies, Fill Location, Round Up, and Round Down.

The system checks to see which replenishment strategy 
 will be used:

- If Fill Location Strategy, 
 then the system will replenish enough product to fill an entire location.

- If Round Up, then the system 
 will round up when replenishing for less than a full increment. If the 
 replenishment amount is for less than a full increment (pallet, case, 
 etc), the system will round up and replenish the full increment. For example, 
 if the replenishment amount is for 1.75 case, the system will replenish 
 2 cases.

- If Round Down, then the system 
 will round down when replenishing for less than a full increment. If the 
 replenishment amount is for less than a full increment (pallet, case, 
 etc), the system will round down and replenish the full increment. For 
 example, if the replenishment amount is for 1.75 case, the system will 
 replenish 1 case.

Step 7: The system uses the allocation rule to select the replenishment's 
 from location(s)

The system determines which allocation rule it will apply to the replenishment 
 quantity. It selects the allocation rule in the following order:

The system attempts to assign the allocation rule defined on the 
 Replenishment Master Record.

If the rule is NOT 
 defined on the Replenishment 
 Master Record, the system will check the Item Record.

If the rule is NOT defined on the Item Record, the system 
 will assign the *Default allocation record.

See the Allocation Process Diagram for more 
 information.

Step 8: Replenishment complete. Replenishment records must be processed 
 by work creation.

The system completes Steps 3 - 7 for all locations that it needs 
 to check.

If this replenishment was run manually 
 (Step 1), the system will automatically run the work creation process 
 (see the Work Creation Process Diagram for more information). The system             will not run the work creation 
 process if the replenishment master is defined to perform immediate execution 
 on replenishment requests. This allows you to run replenishments without 
 creating any work (see the replenishment setup procedures for more information).

If this replenishment was run automatically from 
 a wave (Step 1), the system will run the work creation process, 
 if it's included in the wave step flow (see the Work Creation Process 
 Diagram for more information). If you are running immediate execution 
 replenishment (see bullet above), the system will not need to invoke the 
 work creation process.

If this replenishment is set for no work creation (Step 1), the system will allocate the inventory and generate replenishment requests for eligible locations, execute those requests (which marks the quantity On Hand at the destination location), and then generate a Replenishment Pick List (if paperwork is setup properly). This document would then be used to perform the actual inventory movements.

The replenishment criteria record is defined on the replenishment master

The system selects the possible

It sorts the selected locations

 Height / Item Height), whichever is greater.

 defined on the Replenishment 
 Master Record, the system will check the Item Record.

                
 

            

            

                
If the rule is NOT defined on the Item Record, the system 
 will assign the *Default allocation record.

Replenishment to Satisfy Location Need...

        
 

        
This process diagram illustrates how the system creates replenishment

The replenishment process creates work requests to accommodate replenishments. 
 Replenishment can be initiated manually from the Inventory Insight or 
 it can be part of the wave cycle.

        
 

        
 

        
Step 1: Replenishment is initiated from either the wave cycle or the Inventory Insight.

        

            

                
If the replenishment is initiated 
 from a wave, the system retrieves all of the replenishment master 
 records with the 'wave' replenishment mode. It sorts the records in priority 
 order. Later, these records are processed in priority order: the lower 
 the priority number, the sooner it is run.

                
 

            

            
If the replenishment 
 is initiated from the Inventory Insight, the system will display 
 the Manual Replenishment screen. The user will select the replenishment 
 master records that he/she wants to run.

        

        
 

        
Step 2: The system uses the Replenishment Criteria record to identify 
 the locations eligible for replenishment and order them.

        
The replenishment criteria record is defined on the replenishment master 
 record.

        

            

                
The system selects the possible 
 replenishment locations based 
 on the values defined on the Filter By Tab on the Replenishment Criteria 
 Window. This tab does not determine which locations will be replenished; 
 rather, it filters through all the warehouse locations and selects which 
 ones might be replenished.

                
 

            

            

                
It sorts the selected locations 
 based on the values defined 
 on the Order By Tab on the Replenishment Criteria Window. If you define 
 multiple values, the system applies them in the order that they appear 
 in the record list. 

                
 

            

        

        
Step 3: The system identifies how much product is in each location.

        

            

                
First, the system identifies which items in the location are eligible 
 for replenishment. It checks the values defined on the Filter By Tab on 
 the Replenishment Item Criteria Window. If an item in the location meets 
 the criteria defined on the replenishment item criteria record, it is 
 considered eligible for replenishment.

                
 

            

            

                
Next, For each eligible item, the system identifies the On Hand 
 and In Transit Quantities associated with the location.

                
 

            

            

                
It references the value in the Replenishment Increment Field on 
 replenishment master record. If the location's UM is different than the 
 record's UM, the system will convert the location's quantity to the UM 
 defined on the replenishment master record.

                
 

            

        

        
Step 4: It determines how many units that location can hold.

        
The system will access the Item Location Capacity record to determine 
 how many units this location can hold. It will reference the Maximum Quantity 
 Field on this window.

        

            

                
If the Maximum Quantity is defined,

 location can hold.

                
 

            

            

                
If the Maximum Quantity is not

It compares the location's dimensions to the item's dimensions. 
 The location dimensions are stored on the location type record. The item 
 dimensions are stored for either the item or its item class on the item 
 unit of measure record.

 Length) x (Location Width / Item Width) x (Location Height / Item Height) 
 or (Location Length / Item Width) x (Location Width / Item Length) x (Location

The system determines if a location should be replenished by completing 
 the following:

        

            

                
The system determines the location's percentage of fullness, by 
 dividing the On Hand and In Transit Quantities (Step 3) by the Maximum 
 Quantity (Step 4).

                
 

            

            

                
It compares this percentage to the value defined in the Minimum 
 Replenishment Threshold Field on the Item Location Capacity record.

                
 

            

            
If this amount is equal to or less than value 
 defined in the Minimum Replenishment Threshold Field, the system will 
 trigger a replenishment for this location.

If a replenishment is required, the system uses the strategies defined 
 on the replenishment master record. Currently, the system supports two 
 strategies, Fill Location and Round Up.

        

            

                
The system checks to see if the 
 Fill Location Strategy is used?

                
 

            

            

                

                    
If yes, the system will 
 set the Maximum Replenishment Fill % to 100%. Note: after the replenishment 
 is complete, this percent reverts back to its original value.

                    
 

                

                

                    
If no, the system will 
 not change the Maximum Replenishment Fill %.

                    
 

                

            

            

                
The system multiplies the Maximum Replenishment Fill % by the location's 
 Maximum Quantity (defined at Step 4). For example, if the Maximum Replenishment 
 Fill % is 75% and the Maximum Quantity is 25, the system would want 18.75 
 units in that location (.75 x 25 = 18.75).

                
 

            

            

                
It subtracts this sum from the location's quantity (On Hand quantity 
 + In Transit quantity). For example, assume that there are 2 units in 
 the location and 1 unit In Transit. The system would subtract the units 
 associated with this location from the number obtained at Step B (18.75) 
 - (2 + 1) = 15.75.

                
 

            

            

                
It checks to see if the Round Up Strategy is used.

                
 

            

            

                

                    
If yes, and the sum 
 is not a whole number, the system will round the replenishment amount 
 up. In the Step C example, the replenishment request is 16.

                    
 

                

                
If no, 
 and the sum is not a whole number, the system will round the replenishment 
 amount down. In the Step C example, the replenishment request is 15.

 from location(s)

 quantity. It selects the allocation rule in the following order:

        

            

                
The system attempts to assign the allocation rule defined on the 
 Replenishment Master Record.

                
 

            

            

                
If the rule is NOT 
 defined on the Replenishment 
 Master Record, the system will check the Item Record.

                
 

            

            

                
If the rule is NOT defined on the Item Record, the system 
 will assign the *Default allocation record.

                
 

            

        

        
See the Allocation Process Diagram for more 
 information.

 by work creation.

This document would then be used to perform the actual inventory movements.
